claims.text: Division I of H.R. 2670 as passed by the Senate on 27 July 2023 was the 'Unidentified Anomalous Phenomena Disclosure Act of 2023', Sections 9001-9010, including a Review Board and eminent domain over recovered technologies of unknown origin.
The enacted FY2024 NDAA (P.L. 118-31) contains Subtitle C, Sections 1841-1843, establishing the UAP Records Collection at NARA without the Review Board or eminent domain provisions.
NDAA FY2025 (P.L. 118-159) Section 6802 is titled 'Sunset of requirements relating to audits of unidentified anomalous phenomena historical record report'.
The dilution of the Schumer-Rounds disclosure language during the FY2024 conference was reported contemporaneously as a deliberate weakening rather than a drafting accident.

connections.edgeLabel: passed one chamber, stripped in conference - the domain's instructive defeat
connections.label: UAP Disclosure Act of 2023 (S.Amdt. 797 to S. 2226; Division G of the Senate-passed FY2024 NDAA)
connections.note: The only text ever passed by a chamber of Congress legislating on the assumption that recovered non-human technology exists and is held in part by private entities. It rode to the Senate floor as an amendment, cleared the Senate as a division of S. 2226, and did not survive conference into P.L. 118-31 in that form. The mechanism of the defeat is the lesson, which is why it belongs to process rather than to statute.

desc: Legislation is where the disclosure fight has produced its only binding outcomes and its most instructive defeats, and the mechanism of the defeats matters more than their fact. The UAP Disclosure Act of 2023, carried as Division I of the Senate-passed FY2024 NDAA with ten sections, would have created an independent Review Board with authority to compel release and an eminent domain provision over recovered technologies of unknown origin held by any person. What emerged from conference and became law in P.L. 118-31 was Subtitle C - a records collection at NARA, a duty to transmit, and postponement grounds - with the Review Board and eminent domain removed. The removal happened in conference, where authorship is diffuse and no recorded vote attaches, which is the characteristic signature of this domain: UAP provisions rarely lose on the floor, they lose in the seam between chambers. The fight continued through the FY2025 NDAA's Section 6802 sunset of the historical-record audit requirements and into the FY2026 and FY2027 cycles. Scoring high on this domain means an entity drafts, sponsors, amends or strips this language - and stripping counts as much as sponsoring.

timeline.label: The Review Board is stripped in conference
timeline.text: P.L. 118-31 is enacted with Subtitle C - a UAP Records Collection at NARA, an agency duty to transmit, and grounds for postponement. The independent Review Board and the eminent domain provision over recovered technologies, both passed by the Senate as Division I of H.R. 2670, are removed in conference where no recorded vote attaches.
